title: Simple Baselines for Image Restoration
grouping: Three captioned panels: (a) 'Multi-Stage Architecture' spans the full width at the top, (b) 'Multi-Scale Fusion Architecture' and (c) 'UNet Architecture (ours)' share the bottom row. Every panel is laid on horizontal bands separated by light-grey dashed rules, one band per spatial size, labelled in the left margin (H x W, H/2 x W/2, H/4 x W/4) under the margin header 'Spatial Size'.
shapes_depth: Every block is the same peach rounded rectangle labelled 'Block' with a subscript repeat count (x n1 ... x n5) in its lower-right corner. Thin black orthogonal arrows; 'input' and 'output' are small text at the line ends. No images, no colour difference between approaches.
proposed_highlight: Only the bold 'ours' in panel (c)'s caption marks the proposal; it is visibly the simplest wiring of the three.
lesson: Compare architecture families on shared horizontal resolution bands (dashed rules labelled H x W, H/2 x W/2, H/4 x W/4 in the margin) with one identical 'Block' box everywhere, so only the wiring differs and the simplest diagram is the proposed one.
notes: elements 'other' = the dashed resolution-band rules with margin labels. It is Figure 2 of the paper (Figure 1 is a PSNR-vs-cost plot), but it plays the teaser role of comparing approaches. Venue from the arXiv comment ('Accepted to ECCV 2022'). The panels are generic architecture families, not a redraw of any one cited model. The figure is embedded in the PDF as one raster image, so photo_share is unknown (null) and the palette is measured over the whole raster.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)

core.what: three inter-block architectures (multi-stage, multi-scale fusion, UNet ours) drawn as identical grids of the same 'Block x n_i' boxes on shared resolution rows, ours last, so only the wiring differs

relations.form: (a) spans the full top width, (b) and (c) sit side by side below; every panel reuses the same peach Block boxes on the same three rows, ours is panel (c) at bottom right
within each panel blocks run left to right, stepping down one dashed resolution row per encoder block and back up on the decoder side
(a) repeats the whole U shape twice left to right, the second U fed by horizontal lines that drop from the first U's decoder blocks
in (b) crossing diagonal lines converge from every encoder block onto points in front of each decoder block, and inputs/outputs enter and leave at every scale
the left margin labels the three rows H x W, H/2 x W/2, H/4 x W/4, separated by grey dashed rules, so vertical position encodes spatial resolution

channels.colour: a single peach fill for every block; colour carries no distinction between panels or block roles
channels.shape: one rounded block shape for all processing; inputs and outputs are only text at arrow ends
channels.line: thin black arrows for all data flow; grey dashed horizontal rules separate resolution levels (structural, not flow)
channels.frame: no frames; panels are separated only by whitespace and their (a)/(b)/(c) captions

quality.strengths: Holding every block identical and the resolution rows fixed across the three panels makes the wiring the only variable, so the extra cross-scale lines of (b) and the doubled U of (a) are visible as geometry against the sparse U of (c); the resolution axis is labelled once at the left and reused.
quality.weaknesses: Ours (c) gets no more space or salience than the baselines and is marked only by bold '(ours)' in its caption; in (a) the long horizontal hand-off lines from the first U to the second run behind other blocks and make tight elbows, and (b)'s diagonals cross into an unreadable bundle.

insights.structure: Three sub-figures (a) multi-stage on top full width, (b) multi-scale fusion and (c) UNet (ours) side by side below, all sharing three resolution rows H x W, H/2 x W/2, H/4 x W/4 separated by dashed horizontal lines labelled on the left.
insights.data: Every stage is the same peach rounded 'Block x n_i' box, so only the wiring differs; inputs and outputs are just text labels at line ends.
insights.emphasis: The proposed design is the sparsest panel and is marked '(ours)' in bold in its caption, contrasting with the crossing lines of (b) and the doubled chain of (a).
insights.flow: Left to right with downward arrows to lower resolutions and upward arrows back; skip lines run horizontally along each resolution row.
insights.avoid: All blocks share one colour and the ours panel has no visual highlight beyond the caption, so the comparison relies entirely on reading wiring.

arrangement.units: three unboxed sub-figures with (a)/(b)/(c) captions below, each a grid of identical block boxes on shared resolution rows
arrangement.shared: the resolution rows and their left-side labels are shared across panels
